# Second-line lipid-lowering agents

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Cardiology and angiology > Relevant pharmacology > Second-line lipid-lowering agents*

[Original Article Link](/library/Ym0nVg)

---

## Summary

Second-line lipid-lowering agents include <u>fibrates</u>, <u>bile acid resins</u>, <u>niacin</u>, and <u>cholesterol</u> absorption inhibitors. These drugs can be used concurrently with <u>statins</u> for patients who have <u>hypercholesterolemia</u> that is inadequately controlled with <u>statin</u> monotherapy. They can also be used as second-line agents for patients who experience persistent side effects from <u>statins</u> (e.g., <u>myositis</u>, <u>myalgias</u>, and/or <u>myopathy</u>). Each drug targets different steps in the <u>cholesterol</u> and lipid metabolism pathways to treat <u>hypercholesterolemia</u> and, therefore, vary in their <u>effectiveness</u> at decreasing <u>low-density lipoprotein</u> (<u>LDL</u>), increasing <u>high-density lipoprotein</u> (<u>HDL</u>), and decreasing <u>triglycerides</u>. Second-line lipid-lowering agents are rarely indicated for <u>primary prevention</u> of cardiovascular disease because they do not improve cardiovascular outcomes or mortality.

## Fibrates (fibric acid derivatives)

* Agents: : bezafibrate, fenofibrate, and gemfibrozil

* Mechanism of action: : activation of the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (<u>PPAR</u>–α) → ↑ <u>lipoprotein lipase</u> activity → more rapid degradation of <u>LDL</u> and <u>triglycerides</u> and induction of <u>HDL</u> synthesis → ↓ <u>LDL</u>, ↑ <u>HDL</u>, ↓↓↓ <u>triglyceride</u>

* Indication: <u>Severe hypertriglyceridemia</u>

* Adverse effects

* <u>Dyspepsia</u>

* <u>Myopathy</u>, especially in combination with <u>statins</u>

* <u>Cholelithiasis</u>: <u>fibrates</u> inhibit <u>cholesterol 7α hydroxylase</u> → decreased <u>bile acid</u> synthesis → supersaturation of <u>bile</u> with <u>cholesterol</u> (↑ <u>cholesterol</u>:<u>bile acid</u> <u>ratio</u>)

* ↑ <u>LFTs</u> (reversible)

* Mild decrease in <u>hemoglobin</u>, <u>hematocrit</u>, and <u>WBC</u> upon initiation; normally stabilizes with long-term therapy

* Contraindications

* <u>Renal insufficiency</u>

* <u>Liver</u> failure

* <u>Gall bladder</u> diseases

* Interactions: enhance the effect of other drugs (e.g., <u>sulfonylureas</u>, <u>warfarin</u>) by inhibiting hepatic <u>CYP450</u>

---

## Bile acid resins

* Drugs: cholestyramine, colestipol, colesevelam

* Mechanism of action
* <u>Ion exchange resin</u> binds <u>bile acids</u> in the intestine;   → interruption of <u>enterohepatic circulation</u> (↓ <u>bile</u> acid absorption and ↑ <u>bile</u> acid excretion);   → ↑ conversion (compensatory) of <u>cholesterol</u> to <u>bile</u> → lowers <u>cholesterol</u> pool in the <u>liver</u> and promotes synthesis of <u>LDL receptors</u> and ↑ <u>LDL receptor</u> recycling → ↓↓ unbound <u>LDL</u>, slightly ↑ <u>HDL</u>, and slightly ↑ <u>triglycerides</u>

* Indications

* Combination treatment with <u>statins</u> in <u>hypercholesterolemia</u>

* Digitoxin overdose

* <u>Pruritus</u> associated with elevated <u>bile acid</u> levels (<u>cholestasis</u>)

* <u>Bile acid diarrhea</u>

* Adverse effects

* Gastrointestinal: <u>nausea</u>, abdominal <u>bloating</u> and cramping

* ↑ <u>LFTs</u>

* <u>Myalgia</u>

* Contraindications

* <u>Hypertriglyceridemia</u> 300–500 mg/dL

* <u>Hypertriglyceridemia</u>-induced <u>pancreatitis</u>

* <u>Bowel obstruction</u>

* <u>Drug interactions</u>: reduces absorption of <u>warfarin</u>, <u>digoxin</u>, and fat-soluble <u>vitamins</u>

---

## Niacin

* Mechanism of action: inhibits <u>lipolysis</u> and <u>fatty acid</u> release in <u>adipose tissue</u> through blockade of <u>hormone</u>-sensitive <u>lipase</u> and ↓ hepatic <u>VLDL</u> synthesis → ↓↓ <u>triglyceride</u>, ↓ <u>LDL</u> synthesis, ↑↑ <u>HDL</u>

* Indication: <u>Severe hypertriglyceridemia</u>

* Adverse effects

* Flushing and <u>pruritus</u>: ↑ <u>prostaglandin</u> synthesis → peripheral <u>vasodilation</u> (pretreatment with <u>aspirin</u> or <u>ibuprofen</u> can minimize this side effect)

* <u>Hyperglycemia</u>

* <u>Hyperuricemia</u> and <u>gout</u> (e.g., <u>podagra</u>)

* <u>Paresthesias</u>

* GI upset (e.g., <u>diarrhea</u>, flatulence, abdominal <u>pain</u>)

* ↑ <u>LFTs</u>

* Contraindications

* <u>Liver</u> failure

* <u>Gout</u>

* Hemorrhage

* <u>Gastric ulcer</u>

* Cardiovascular instability

---

## Ezetimibe

* Mechanism of action: selective inhibition of <u>cholesterol</u> reabsorption at the brush border of <u>enterocytes</u> (<u>cholesterol</u> transporter NPC1L1) → ↓↓ <u>LDL</u>; , little effect on <u>HDL</u> (slight ↑) and <u>triglycerides</u> (slight ↓)

* Indication

* Monotherapy: in contraindications or <u>statin intolerance</u>

* Combination therapy (<u>statin</u> and <u>ezetimibe</u>): in insufficient <u>LDL cholesterol</u> reduction by <u>statins</u>

* Adverse effects: rare, except in combination therapy

* ↑ <u>Liver</u> enzymes

* <u>Angioedema</u>

* <u>Diarrhea</u>

* <u>Myalgia</u>

* Contraindication: coadministration with a <u>statin</u> during active <u>liver</u> disease

---

## PCSK9 inhibitors

* Drugs: alirocumab, evolocumab

* Mechanism of action: <u>monoclonal antibodies</u> that inhibit proprotein convertase subtilisin kexin 9 (<u>PCSK9</u>), an enzyme that degrades the <u>LDL-receptor</u> → increased removal of <u>LDL</u> from the blood stream → ↓↓↓ <u>LDL</u>, ↑ <u>HDL</u>, ↓ <u>triglycerides</u>

* Indication: add-on therapy for patients who have both of the following [[4]](/library/zYXr79)

* <u>LDL</u> â¥ 70 mg/dL (â¥ 1.8 mmol/L) despite maximally tolerated treatment with <u>statins</u> and <u>ezetimibe</u>

* Presence of very high-risk <u>atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease</u>

* Adverse effects: <u>myalgia</u> [[5]](/library/rsXfwz)

---

## Others

### Marine <u>omega-3 fatty acids</u> (fish oil)




* Mechanism of action: : most likely decreases transportation of free <u>fatty acids</u> to the <u>liver</u> and inhibits <u>triglyceride</u>-synthesizing enzymes → slight ↑ of <u>HDL</u> and <u>LDL</u> and (at higher doses) ↓ <u>triglycerides</u>

* Adverse effects

* Fishy <u>taste</u>

* <u>Nausea</u>





### Lomitapide




* Mechanism of action: inhibits <u>microsomal triglyceride transfer protein</u> (<u>MTTP</u>) → ↓ <u>VLDL</u>, <u>LDL</u>, and <u>chylomicrons</u>

* Indications: <u>homozygous</u> <u>familial hypercholesterolemia</u>

* Adverse effects: gastrointestinal symptoms (<u>nausea</u>, <u>vomiting</u>), elevation of <u>transaminases</u>
